concepts.concept: Direct-bypass decision (whether a host request bypasses the cache and is served directly)

confidentiality.reason: The direct-bypass decision drives bus_req_o.stb (line 187), an external output that reveals the decision to the bus/receiver.

integrity.reason: ctrl_nxt.buf_dir is set from host request fields (address nibble, amo, debug) in S_IDLE (line 173), so an external requester can change this decision.

availability.reason: The stored decision (ctrl.buf_dir) is latched from ctrl_nxt on every rising clock edge (ctrl <= ctrl_nxt at line 126) and there is no external stall gating that latch.

undermined behavior.reason: The comb process provides the only drivers for the decision (default at line 140 and conditional set at line 173); no debug/test override or alternate driver exists.

undermined behavior.reason: The decoded fields are driven only by the state-machine assignments in S_LOOKUP (e.g. tag at line 180) and the download increment (line 244); there is no debug/test override that substitutes a different source.

concepts.concept: Cache clear / fence command that invalidates cache state and (optionally) issues a bus fence

confidentiality.reason: The fence/clear is generated in response to the host's fence request and forwarded as bus_req_o.fence (line 217); this is a request the writer already initiated and therefore reveals nothing new to that writer.

integrity.reason: The clear/fence path is driven from the host fence input (ctrl_nxt.buf_sync <= ... host_req_i.fence at line 138), so an external requester can cause the clear and (when configured) the bus fence.

availability.reason: When the controller enters S_CLEAR it asserts cache_o.cmd_clr (line 219) and then returns to S_IDLE (line 221); there is no external stall/gate that prevents issuance of the clear command apart from global reset/clock.

undermined behavior.reason: The bus fence assertion is conditional on the static READ_ONLY generic (line 217), so a configuration mode disables the bus fence behavior.
